AUTHOR: Kitchingman
TITLE: Fish use of restored mangroves matches that in natural mangroves regardless of forest age
REGION: Moreton Bay, southeast Queensland, Australia (restored and natural mangroves)
SPECIES: yellowfin bream, sea mullet, common toadfish, common silverbiddy (targets) + sand whiting, crescent grunter, moses snapper, banded toadfish, weeping toadfish
DATA: Own unbaited remote underwater video (SJCAM), 280 h footage; 255 training snippets (13,928 annotations); test 76 videos (4,112 annotations)
V_EV: Study site: 'Depth at the fringe cameras was 0.8 m at the top of the tide'; training snippets 'at different turbidity levels'
D2: 80/20 train/validation; test = videos of 1 of 5 cameras per site-zone excluded from training
D_EV: DL Model: 'test dataset that contained 4,112 fish annotations from 76 videos of 1 of the 5 cameras (per site-zone combination) that was excluded from the training'
R_EV: DL Model: test videos from '1 of the 5 cameras (per site-zone combination)' of the same 2021 survey campaign
C_EV: Abundance Predictions: 'species-specific confidence threshold of 95, 90, 70, and 60%'; 'sequential nonmaximum suppression to minimize false detections'
E_EV: DL Model: 'We determined the performance of the DL model using the F1 score on abundance estimates ... which in our case was MaxN'
ARCH: Deep learning object detector (architecture not stated; transfer learning from Ditria et al. 2021 model) + Seq-NMS
METR: F1 on MaxN; mean MaxN per 20-min; ANOVA, Spearman correlation
NOTE: Unbaited RUV coded as BRUV category (RUV). Held-out camera (one of five per site-zone) = video/deployment-level split within same campaign (D=Y, R=N per P2). Seq-NMS spatiotemporal filter coded as explicit duplicate/false-detection handling mechanism (C5), giving C_ALL=Y with reported thresholds; thresholds also justified as minimising FP/FN. Transfer learning from previously trained southeast Queensland fish model (PRE=수중 데이터셋). Detector architecture not named in main text. Per-species F1 in Table S3 (supplement not in text).
